title: Top Five Games I Sold and Bought Again
body:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=qqQxwunPfLo

A list about regret, and quietly the most autobiographical video Daniel (@dungeondive) has made in a while: five games he sold and then bought back.

Fifth is **Dungeoneer**, Thomas Denmark's card-based crawl from the early 2000s, where moving between rooms generates glory points you spend on yourself and peril points your opponents spend against you — a competitive engine he says still hasn't been replicated. Fourth is **Space Hulk**, the first big-box game he bought with his own money in high school, sold when he moved to Southern California to chase music, rebought at fourth edition and still the best-produced game he owns. Third is **Kingdom Death: Monster**, sold at a hefty profit during the out-of-print spike to fund a DSI Pro 2 synthesizer he still loves, then rebought at 1.5 to fill what he calls a KDM-shaped hole. Second is Plaid Hat's **Dungeon Run**, semi-co-op until the boss dies and the MacGuffin turns it into tag.

First is **Arkham Horror 2nd Edition**, his reintroduction to the hobby — impenetrable until Universal Head's rules summaries made it click. He sold it, replaced it with Eldritch Horror and Elder Sign, and eventually bought a complete collection back. The purchase that prompted the list.

----

Selling to fund another hobby, then buying it all back later. Which sale do you still regret?
